title: Real world MCPs in GitHub Copilot Agent Mode — Jon Peck, Microsoft
talk_summary: Jon Peck demonstrates GitHub Copilot agent mode using MCP servers to connect to Postgres and GitHub, with permission prompts and read-only DB access. He recommends complete README/specs, explicit MCP naming, and pre-injected instructions including changelog requirements.

takeaways.technique: Standard MCP tool servers for external systems
takeaways.what_they_do: Configure MCP servers in the agent environment so the agent can call external data/tools through a standard protocol instead of bespoke shell/CLI glue. The agent parses the prompt, selects an MCP, asks permission, then calls it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Copilot itself parses that prompt and identifies the fact that it should be using an MCP for this connection

takeaways.technique: Read-only DB MCP for agent data access
takeaways.what_they_do: Use a Postgres MCP server that only supports read-only queries so the agent can pull schema/data for mocks without mutating the database.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this one only functions in readonly mode, which is one of the reasons I like it because it's very safe

takeaways.technique: Pre-injected agent instructions plus changelog requirement
takeaways.what_they_do: Put standards, security checks, and a changelog instruction in a file injected into every prompt so the agent consistently follows them and records what it did.
takeaways.evidence_quote: include a change log of everything you've done

takeaways.technique: Explicitly name the tool/MCP in prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: When the agent does not reliably infer the right tool, the speaker explicitly names the MCP and operation in the prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: So I've taken to just being explicit.

takeaways.technique: GitHub MCP for branch and PR creation
takeaways.what_they_do: After code changes, the agent uses the GitHub MCP to create a branch, commit changes, and open a PR in one flow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: go ahead and use the GitHub MCP to commit all of these changes to a new branch and make a PR

takeaways.what_they_do: Write a very complete README with project structure, env vars, schema, API endpoints, and diagrams before asking the agent to implement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that readme is intended to be very complete
